title: Digital Gold: Unlocking a $700-Billion Opportunity
gist: World Gold Council estimates digital and tokenised gold, a $45-55 billion category under 1% of the ~$13 trillion physical investment gold market, could unlock up to $700 billion of latent demand and reach $160-170 billion by 2031 if trust, access, utility and pricing barriers are met.

insights.claim: Physical investment gold is worth about $13 trillion, while digital gold (vaulted and tokenised) is below 1% of it and has grown into a $45-55 billion category.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Tokenised gold is small but at an inflection point.

insights.claim: Tokenised gold generated $90 billion of cumulative spot trading volume in Q1 2026, more than in all of 2025.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council

insights.claim: Fully realised, up to $700 billion of latent digital gold demand would broadly match physically-backed gold ETFs today; the base case is about 27% CAGR to $160-170 billion by 2031.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Sets the WGC's sizing for tokenised gold growth; assumes all else equal including gold price.

insights.claim: Nearly 9 in 10 of 12,000+ surveyed retail investors signal willingness to invest in digital gold under the right conditions, but this is not yet converting at scale.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Gap between interest and adoption is the opportunity.

insights.claim: Trust is the swing factor: nearly four in five investors want to trust the provider first, and a clear path to redeem for physical gold and regulation and consumer protection are key.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Regulated, redeemable products are likely to win share.

insights.claim: Where digital gold is embedded in super-apps, payment platforms and banking apps, as in India, China and Indonesia, penetration is up to seven times higher.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Distribution through fintech channels drives adoption.

insights.claim: Yield generation via lending or collateral use is the top-cited unique selling point, ahead of payments, pointing to a shift beyond gold as store of value.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Yield-bearing gold products could be a growth niche.

insights.claim: An uncompetitive price versus physical gold and gold ETFs is the second most common barrier to entry.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Fee compression will matter for tokenised gold issuers.

insights.claim: Around 65% of latent demand comes from people who have not yet invested in gold, and more than half of existing gold holders would fund digital gold with money not currently allocated to gold.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Digital gold is likely to bring new money rather than cannibalise bars, coins or ETFs.

insights.claim: Awareness of digital gold is 50% among 25-34-year-olds versus 23% among those 55 and older, and younger cohorts are twice as likely to invest if barriers are addressed.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
